description: A limix rules document: REST and/or GraphQL access rules. Unknown top-level keys are rejected; keys starting with `x-` are accepted for YAML anchors and dropped.

limix.description: The version of the rules format. Always 1.

global.description: Settings applied across the whole document.

rest.description: REST rules, keyed by path pattern then HTTP method (`*` for any). The first rule whose pattern matches the request path, in document order, is used.

graphql.description: GraphQL rules, keyed by type name then field name (`*` for every other field of the type). Query, Mutation and Subscription cover root fields; any other type name targets fields on that type wherever it appears.

__schema1.description: Prefix prepended to every REST path pattern, e.g. "/api".

__schema3.description: What a REST request, or a GraphQL root field, that no rule names is answered. "allow" lets it through; "deny" makes the file the exhaustive statement of what the service exposes: an unnamed path is refused, 401 for an anonymous caller and 403 otherwise. Required, so that leaving a door open is a decision written down.

__schema4.description: Path pattern: `:name` for one segment, `*name` or `*` for the rest, `{...}` optional, e.g. "/users/:id".

__schema5.description: Rules keyed by HTTP method for this path pattern.

relations.description: Per-object relation checks, one rung after the other: the first that fails denies, which is how the 404-then-403 ladder is written.

anyOf.description: Roles in disjunctive normal form: the OUTER list is OR, the INNER list is AND, so [["admin"], ["editor", "reviewer"]] reads "admin, or editor and reviewer". A role holds when it is in claims.roles.

Permissions in disjunctive normal form: the OUTER list is OR, the INNER list is AND, so [["a"], ["b", "c"]] reads "a, or b and c". A permission holds when it is in claims.scope (space separated) and, when the caller carries a claims.permissions list, also in that list.
Names of conditions registered in code (compilePolicy({ conditions })). Every named condition must hold. An unknown name fails at compile time.

__schema16.description: Declares that the rule needs a signed-in caller and nothing more. Cannot be combined with `public: true`.

__schema18.description: Lets anonymous callers reach the rule. Only for routes that carry their own credential. Cannot be combined with `authenticated: true`, `roles`, `permissions`, `when` or `relations`.

require.description: Requirement in disjunctive normal form: the OUTER list is OR, the INNER list is AND, so [[A, B], [C]] reads "(A and B) or C".

onDeny.description: How a failure of this rung is answered. NOT_FOUND (the default) is the same answer as for an id that never existed; FORBIDDEN is for a second rung on an object the caller can already see.

code.description: The refusal's code, replacing the default one of the answer. Put it under "auth.errors." for @softistx/alxia-access to read it.

relation.description: The relation the caller must hold, e.g. "view" or "edit".

type.description: The type of the object, e.g. "bookmark".

from.description: Where the object id is read from: "param.<name>", "query.<name>" or "json.<path>" (dotted). A path resolving to a list requires the relation on every element. Defaults to "param.id".

__schema36.description: Any method. A method written beside it wins on the same pattern.

__schema37.description: Type name: Query, Mutation or Subscription for root fields, any other name for fields of that type wherever it appears.

propertyNames.description: Field name on this GraphQL type, e.g. "createUser", or `*` for every other field.

relations.description: Per-object relation checks, one rung after the other. Ids are read from `args.<path>` or `source.<path>`.
